text:
alex: Quick design proposal for a new synthetic traffic harness to exercise kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV-cache behavior, and long-tail latency shaping. Goals: deterministic apples-to-apples perf comparisons, controllable tail sculpting, repeatable cache warmup, and clear measurement boundaries. WIP sketch below.

maria: +1. Can you list the traffic primitives? want to make sure we cover prefix-heavy requests vs full-seq.

alex: primitives: steady qps; short micro-bursts (3-10s spike); burst trains (N bursts separated by pauses); heavy-tail interarrival (Pareto/Weibull); seq-length mixes (short/medium/long); KV-prefetch vs cold-start flows; replayed traces with synthetic jitter. Also a warmup phase that pins KV entries.

samir: for KV cache we need: repeated-prefix sequences, random-prefix eviction patterns, and multi-turn sessions that reuse KV across requests. Suggest adding session_id to tie KV across X requests so we can measure cross-request hit ratio.

alex: implementation sketch: small Go harness using goroutines + leaky-bucket rate limiter, YAML scenario configs and a replay mode. Example config snippet: 

```
traffic:
  - name: steady
    qps: 50
    duration_s: 600
  - name: micro_burst
    pattern: burst
    peak_qps: 200
    burst_len_s: 3
    cooldown_s: 7
  - name: heavy_tail
    pattern: pareto
    alpha: 1.5
    duration_s: 1800
```

kevin: How do we ensure apples-to-apples between kernels? Need fully deterministic env: fixed model weights, same RNG seeds, flush OS/GPU caches between runs, consistent batcher config, and a KV warmup phase. Measure token-level latency and percentiles (p50/p95/p99/p999). Also capture batch-size distribution over time.

maria: add an explicit "kernel-forcing" mode that pins the selected kernel/compiler path so we can run the identical workload with kernel A vs kernel B without autoswitching. Model variant pinning + batcher seeding.

ops_sarah: FYI perf-bot flagged a regression earlier: job 1782101000 showed n10-rt p99 jump 210ms -> 380ms. We should wire regression detection: auto-open ticket when p99 increases >20% and p999 > threshold.

perf-bot: CI Job "synth-harness/regression" completed. summary: baseline p99 210ms -> new 376ms (+79%). artifacts: https://ci.redwood/synth/1782106789/logs (sampled traces included).

samir: For long-tail shaping use Pareto(alpha=1.5) for interarrival, cap maximum pause to avoid pathological waits. Also overlay scheduled event bursts (ex: holiday window) by multiplying baseline QPS by a factor for a defined window.

alex: Metrics to export: request_ts, kernel_selected, batch_size, kv_hit (true/false), seq_len, latency_ms, tokens_generated, queue_time_ms. Export streams to Prometheus and JSONL dumps per run. Include trace_id for sampling and full traces for regressions.

kevin: Also include a batching heuristics matrix: continuous batching ON/OFF, max_batch_size variations, latency SLO target toggle. Add a "backpressure" knob that introduces artificial slow downstream hosts to exercise the adaptive batcher.

maria: I'll draft the YAML schema and a small runner in workspace/fuzz-testing. want to pair tomorrow to map scenarios to infra and define CI gates.

alex: SGTM. I'll knock up a PoC that replays a 1hr prod sample with jitter + micro-bursts and produces the JSONL metrics + Prom metrics. Expect PR by EOD Friday. :rocket: 

kevin: :thumbsup: Let's also add a short checklist in the PR template: env pinning, seed, cache flush steps, baseline artifacts link, kernel-forcing instructions, and an analysis notebook for p99/p999 deltas.

maria: cool. i'll add the checklist to the testing README and include an example of how to reproduce the perf-bot run locally.

alex: Thanks everyone — this should help isolate whether regressions come from kernel selection vs batching vs cache behavior.

ops_sarah: filing follow-up doc on alert thresholds and ownership after we see the PoC results.

perf-bot: reminder: regression tickets auto-close after 7 days if no new failures reported.

alex: ok closing thread for now, will post PR link when ready.
